gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height that carries well on screens, so you can let the body size lead. Noto Sans Soyombo sits under Edo SZ, whose lowercase stands tall like cast iron capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Edo SZ draws every line with one constant stroke, no pinched joins and no swelling bowls. And Noto Sans Sundanese, clean and open in its e crossbars, sits close to the cap height beneath it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Approachable and clean, Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in its curves and keeps its ascender stems short on tall lowercase bodies. Edo SZ above it cuts every line to a single depth, like an engraver.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Professional in manner, Noto Sans Syloti Nagri has short ascenders, a tall x-height and an a whose lower bowl opens up. Over many lines it reads quick and plain.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Bent-paperclip lines, all one thickness: that's Edo SZ, with lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Syriac follows with blown-glass bowls and easy s turns, friendly line after line.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Edo SZ is all wire and iron, its horizontals as thick as its verticals and its lowercase standing tall. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern sets tall lowercase against small caps, and its curve endings keep their distance.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Noto Sans Syriac Western reads modern and crisp, its terminals held far from the stroke. Edo SZ above it is an outline of constant, heavy ink, so the two feel built from different materials.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Clean is the first impression of Noto Sans Tagalog, whose middle zone dominates each line and whose curves stay generous. And Edo SZ does its best work as a display voice with no hairline-to-stem shift, while the body carries the text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Edo SZ stands up top with lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals and a constant pen pressure. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa follows with open curves and clear gaps, its lowercase filling most of the height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: A plain stripe of constant ink, that's Edo SZ. Noto Sans Tai Le is its quiet partner, strokes tapering out before they touch and almost no step from capital to lowercase.
